name: Short-Term Memory and Compaction
question: How does the agent keep the thread?
summary: Short-term memory is the working state of one session: messages, tool results and plans. When it outgrows the window, the agent clears stale tool results, compacts old turns into a summary, or writes progress notes, while keeping identifiers, amounts, decisions and open tasks intact.
useCases: Sessions that run for dozens or hundreds of turns
Agents whose tool results (search pages, statements, logs) are large
Tasks that must survive a restart or a context limit

items.detail: drop old tool outputs, keep the last few (Claude: keep 3 by default)
summarize old turns into one block (Claude: triggers at 150k by default)
say what must survive: IDs, amounts, dates, decisions, open tasks
a file or row the agent re-reads after each compaction
persist thread state by session ID (LangGraph, Agents SDK Sessions)
each clear rewrites the prefix; clear fewer, larger chunks

steps: Persist the thread by session ID and log input tokens per turn
Clear stale tool results past a trigger, keeping the last few and protecting still-needed tools
Compact old turns with instructions that keep IDs, amounts, decisions and open tasks
Quiz the agent on early-session facts after each compaction
pitfalls: A summary that paraphrases account numbers or amounts
Dropping the first message, which holds the task and constraints
Clearing a little on every turn, which invalidates the prompt cache each time
remember: Clear the bulk, summarize the rest, keep the IDs.
caption: Illustrative session: 4.5k tokens a turn. Clearing at 60k plus compaction keeps context under 70k for 120 turns.

steps.title: Persist the thread
steps.text: Store the messages by session ID so a two-hour call survives restarts. The first message holds the task and constraints; it stays pinned.

steps.title: Measure growth
steps.text: Log input tokens every turn. Each turn adds about 1k of talk and a 3.5k statement or schedule, so the context passes 150k by turn 33.

steps.title: Clear stale tool results
steps.text: Past the trigger, old tool results are replaced by placeholders; the last 3 stay, and get_loan_summary is excluded because the agent still refers to it.

steps.title: Compact with instructions
steps.text: When the conversation itself grows too long, older turns become one summary. The instructions say what must be copied exactly.

steps.title: Keep a progress note
steps.text: After a compaction the agent re-reads a short note of decisions and open tasks, so work carries on from the right place.

steps.title: Check what survived
steps.text: Probe the agent with questions about early turns. If the loan account or EMI is wrong, fix the instructions before shipping.

pros: Lets sessions run far beyond the context window
Tool-result clearing is low risk: results can be fetched again
Compaction instructions let you name what must survive
Lower tokens per turn means lower cost and latency
cons: Summaries can paraphrase or drop exact values
Every clear or compaction rewrites the prefix and invalidates the prompt cache
Repeated compaction can drift from the original
Needs probes to prove early facts survived
avoidWhen: Short, single-task sessions that never approach the limit
Facts that must persist across sessions (use semantic memory)

playgroundGuide.scenario: A housing-finance restructuring call runs 120 turns. Each turn adds about 1k tokens of conversation and one tool result: a statement, an EMI schedule or a bureau pull. The window is 200k. Five early facts must survive: loan account, agreed EMI, NEFT mandate, restructuring date and co-borrower name.

practice.scenario: A housing-finance company’s restructuring assistant handles two-hour calls: statements, EMI schedules and bureau pulls arrive as large tool results. Old results are cleared once context passes a trigger, keeping the last three, and older turns are compacted with instructions to keep the loan account number, the agreed EMI and the pending NEFT mandate verbatim. After each compaction a check asks the agent for those three values.

industries.use: Keep loan account, agreed EMI and mandate status through long calls
Clear bulky log dumps once the root cause is recorded
Compact a long itinerary chat but keep PNRs and fares exactly

practice.analogy: A court stenographer’s minutes. The full transcript goes to the archive; the judge works from minutes that keep every case number, amount and order word for word.

library.name: Anthropic SDK (context editing, compaction)
library.what: Server-side tool-result clearing (clear_tool_uses_20250919) and compaction (compact_20260112) configured per request.

practice.note: Both features are in beta; check the current beta header names in the docs. Persist messages by session ID in your own store.

samples.code:
import anthropic
client = anthropic.Anthropic()

KEEP = ("Summarize the conversation so far. Copy verbatim: loan account numbers, "
        "amounts, dates, EMI and mandate details, decisions made and open tasks.")

def turn(messages, tools):
    r = client.beta.messages.create(
        model="claude-sonnet-4-5",               # use your current model
        max_tokens=2048,
        betas=["context-management-2025-06-27", "compact-2026-01-12"],
        messages=messages, tools=tools,
        context_management={"edits": [
            {"type": "clear_tool_uses_20250919",
             "trigger": {"type": "input_tokens", "value": 100_000},
             "keep": {"type": "tool_uses", "value": 3},
             "clear_at_least": {"type": "input_tokens", "value": 20_000},
             "exclude_tools": ["get_loan_summary"]},
            {"type": "compact_20260112",
             "trigger": {"type": "input_tokens", "value": 150_000},
             "instructions": KEEP},
        ]},
    )
    messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": r.content})  # keeps the compaction block
    return r

numericDrill.question: A session has 40 tool results of 3,500 tokens each. Clearing keeps the last 3 results. How many tokens of tool results are cleared?

interview.question: What is the difference between clearing tool results and compaction?
interview.answer: Clearing removes old tool outputs, which can be re-fetched, and keeps the call record; it is one of the safest reductions. Compaction summarizes the conversation itself, so it needs instructions that keep IDs, amounts, decisions and open tasks.

interview.question: Why clear in large steps rather than a little every turn?
interview.answer: Every change to earlier content invalidates the prompt cache from that point. Clearing at least a large amount at a time (clear_at_least) means fewer cache rewrites for the same saving.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the summary paraphrase account numbers and amounts
mistakes.fix: Instruct the summary to copy identifiers, amounts and open tasks verbatim
Pin the task and constraints; compact the middle

quiz.question: A loan-restructuring call adds about 4.5k tokens a turn, starting from 4k. At which turn does the context first exceed 150k?
A troubleshooting session carries 40 log dumps of 3,500 tokens each. Clearing keeps the last 3. How many tokens are cleared?
quiz.explanation: 37 results × 3,500 = 129,500 tokens.

quiz.question: Which should a compaction summary for a two-hour loan call copy verbatim? Select all that apply.
quiz.explanation: Identifiers and amounts must survive exactly; greetings and small talk can go.

quiz.question: Why is clearing old tool results considered one of the safest context reductions?
options: The model never needs old results
The call stays recorded and the data can be fetched again
It never affects the prompt cache
quiz.explanation: Clearing replaces results with placeholders while the call remains, so nothing is irrecoverable.

quiz.question: A trimming function uses messages.pop(0) whenever the history is too long. What goes wrong?
options: It drops the first message, which holds the task and constraints
It keeps too many tool results
quiz.explanation: The first message usually holds the task; it must be pinned or carried into the summary.

quiz.question: Claude’s tool-result clearing (clear_tool_uses_20250919) keeps how many recent tool uses by default?
quiz.explanation: The default keep value is 3 tool uses.

quiz.question: A claims agent clears a little context on every turn and its prompt-cache hit rate collapses. Which fixes help? Select all that apply.
options: Clear in fewer, larger steps using clear_at_least
Raise the clearing trigger so it runs less often
Clear one tool result on every turn
Move the system prompt to the end of the prompt
quiz.explanation: Every clear rewrites the prefix. Fewer, larger clears protect the cache; the other two make it worse.

quiz.question: Claude’s compaction strategy (compact_20260112) triggers at what input size by default?
quiz.explanation: The default trigger is 150,000 input tokens, with a minimum of 50,000.

quiz.question: After compaction, a clinic assistant answers “Your appointment is next week” instead of “Tuesday 14:30 with Dr Rao”. What is the most likely cause?
options: The summary instructions did not require exact values
quiz.explanation: Generic summaries paraphrase. Instructions must name the values to copy verbatim.

quiz.question: A session sends 20 turns of 10k, 20k … 200k input tokens (growing 10k a turn). What is the total input?
Which are valid ways to keep thread state for a long-running delivery agent? Select all that apply.
options: A LangGraph checkpointer keyed by thread ID
Relying on the model to remember previous API calls
Storing nothing and resending only the last message
quiz.explanation: Checkpointers and Sessions persist state; models are stateless between calls.

quiz.question: When you pass Claude’s compaction response back, what must happen to the compaction block?
options: Drop it and keep the original messages
Append the response content, including the compaction block, to the messages
Convert it to a system prompt
Send it only once per day
quiz.explanation: Append the full response content; the API uses the compaction block in place of earlier content.

quiz.question: A 120-turn session sends 19.8M input tokens unmanaged and 6.4M with clearing and compaction. About what percentage is saved?
A tutoring agent keeps a “progress note” file. When should it re-read it?
options: Only at the start of the course
quiz.explanation: Re-reading the note after compaction restores decisions and open tasks the summary may compress.

quiz.question: Anthropic lists techniques for long-horizon tasks. Which are among them? Select all that apply.
quiz.explanation: Compaction, notes and sub-agents are the named techniques; temperature does not manage context.

quiz.question: Which tool should be listed in exclude_tools when clearing results in a loan call?
options: A search tool whose old results are no longer used
get_loan_summary, which the agent keeps referring to
quiz.explanation: Exclude tools whose results are still referenced; clear the rest.

quiz.question: Anthropic reported that context editing cut token use in a 100-turn web-search evaluation by about how much?
quiz.explanation: Anthropic reported an 84% reduction in token consumption for that evaluation.

quiz.question: A rebooking chat is compacted 7 times in one session and fare details start to drift. What is the best structural fix?
options: Clear bulky tool results first so compaction runs less often
quiz.explanation: Clearing the bulk reduces how often history must be summarized, and each summary-of-a-summary risks drift.

quiz.question: Which checks show that a compaction policy is safe to ship? Select all that apply.
options: Comparing answers with an uncompacted baseline
Checking only that the summary is shorter
Counting how many summaries were written
quiz.explanation: Probes and baseline comparison test what survived; length and counts do not.

quiz.question: A session’s context grows 1k of talk plus a 3k tool result per turn. Clearing keeps only the last 2 results. After 50 turns, with no compaction and a 4k pinned start, what is the context?
quiz.explanation: Pinned 4k + 50 turns of talk (50k) + 2 results × 3k (6k) = 60k.
